object: Pulley animation keyframes, shot from over the water so the travel is never occluded
lens: Shared rig, orthographic lens, one fixed camera (8.6, 5.6, 3.8) for all five moments, ortho scale 5.2

Pulley_Idle.content: restrained pendulum sway of the hanging bucket only

Pulley_Lower.content: crank/drum rotate, rope lengthens, bucket descends to the water-contact socket

Pulley_Lift.content: reverse travel ending with a micro-settle at the taut rest hang

idle.notes: Sway is subtle and pivots at the hook; rope and frame stay still.

lowering.notes: Mid-travel: rope visibly longer, crank rotated, bucket clear of deck and ledge; rope, hook, and bail remain attached (linear-linked channels).

water_contact.notes: Bucket unmistakably in the water with the waterline crossing its lower staves; contact matches the water_contact_socket at local z -0.50.

lifting.notes: Reverse travel mirrors the descent with no rope divergence and no crank/crossbeam contact after the outboard shift.

settled.notes: Bucket returns to the taut rest hang at 0.88 with the micro-settle; crank returns to zero; nothing clips.

defectsFoundAndFixed: The water-contact proof was first shot from the deck side, where the deck edge occluded the moment of contact — reshot from over the water.
The exact contact keyframe read as a hover (base kissing the surface); the banked proof uses the fully dipped final Lower frame so contact is unmistakable.
Clearance math showed the crank grip could graze the crossbeam end mid-rotation; the crank arm and grip moved outboard.
